chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man shaking hands with a woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for a man to shake hands with a woman, except for a woman whom he is forbidden to marry (due to close kinship), such as a sister, daughter, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, or daughter of a sister, or similar. As for the woman whom it is permissible for him to marry, he should not shake her hand except from behind the garment, and he should not squeeze her palm.'

key_terms.مُصَافَحَة: Handshaking or physical contact of hands
key_terms.يَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَتَزَوَّجَهَا: Forbidden for him to marry (referring to close kinship/mahram)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on men shaking hands with non-mahram women?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the general prohibition of handshaking with non-mahram women, a ruling widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as a measure of modesty (haya). It provides a nuanced exception for close female relatives (mahram) and specifies that for other women, contact must be indirect ('from behind clothing') and gentle ('without squeezing'), reflecting the scholarly emphasis on avoiding both physical impurity and emotional temptation.
